reviewPolicy: Entries whose complete runtime-relevant rules are represented by Affliction Forge 0.1.53 may ship as full. Long-term recurrence may use explicit manual reapplication. Bonechill, Brain Worms, and Crimson Ooze are intentionally classified as manual exceptions rather than drivers for new generic engine subsystems; their unsupported source rules must be surfaced as explicit GM comments when those entries are later published.

notes: Stage 2 and 3 speed penalties use Affliction Forge 0.1.52 numeric PF2e modifiers.
The alternate cure by amputating affected limbs is handled manually and is not an engine blocker.
Muscle spasms are descriptive; the rules-facing Stage 3 condition is paralyzed.
Carrier status is descriptive/transmission metadata and is not an engine blocker.
The remaining blocker is the pre-action check that can prevent concentrate spells or item activations.
Later recurrence is handled by manually reapplying the same definition.
Stage 3 uses a 1d20-minute periodic stage effect that reapplies 1d6 persistent bleed damage.
Affliction Forge 0.1.51 already covers the cold-damage healing lock.
Intentional manual exception: environment severity shifting is not planned as a generic Affliction Forge feature.
entries.manualComment: In stages 3 and 4, effects of cold temperatures are one severity step worse for the victim. This environmental severity rewrite is intentionally left for the GM rather than added as a generic Affliction Forge subsystem.

notes: Hoarse voice in Stage 1 is descriptive; Stage 3 uses the speak capability restriction.
Stage 4 uses component-specific persistence so blindness is permanent while enfeebled 2 remains stage-bound.
The published slashing-damage version is represented; optional bludgeoning or piercing variants can be made as editable copies.
Damage-triggered secondary Will saves are handled by Affliction Forge 0.1.50 event reactions.
Affliction Forge 0.1.50 covers the damage-triggered secondary Will saves.
Intentional manual exception: confusion attack rewriting and the special confused-ending rule are not planned as generic engine behavior.
entries.manualComment: When confusion forces attacks, those attacks must become bites; at the later stage, taking damage does not end confused. These confusion-behavior overrides are intentionally handled manually.

The disease tracks one infected hand: using it can cause persistent bleed damage, later the hand becomes unusable and can be permanently lost, and the final confused stage is not ended by damage. These body-part and confusion exceptions are intentionally handled manually.
notes: The alternate cure by amputation before stage 4 is a manual cure option, not an engine blocker.
Intentional manual exception: infected-hand use, hand usability/loss, and the special confused-ending rule are not planned as generic engine behavior.
